title: Work IQ: long-running tasks for A2A and MCP agents
summary: Hold: the briefing says developers opt in and reassures other tenants that nothing needs enabling, although Microsoft has not documented how this capability arrives. The roadmap facts, billing controls and updated consumption-monitoring guidance are supported; the setup and group-policy notes also need small qualifications.

claims.quote: Enable durable long-running A2A and MCP tasks with progress tracking, later result retrieval, and cancellation.

claims.claim: An API or automation call for Work IQ MCP tenant policy is not yet documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Work IQ MCP" policy Graph API PowerShell tenant settings management endpoint. Opened policy-governance-mcp and MCP overview; results describe settings and UI but provide no policy-management endpoint or cmdlet.

claims.claim: The initial Work IQ MCP policy control is tenant-level on/off, without per-user, per-app or per-agent controls.
claims.quote: Tenant-level control applies across the tenant. Per-user, per-app, per-agent, or scenario-specific policy templates aren't part of the initial policy control surface.

claims.claim: A Work IQ MCP policy change can take up to 24 hours to apply across the tenant.
claims.quote: After you save the setting, it can take up to 24 hours for the policy change to apply across your tenant.

claims.claim: The MCP policy documentation does not confirm its application to A2A or describe the specific long-running-task feature.
claims.quote: Searched: "Work IQ" task resume policy spending policy audit cancellation administrator. Opened policy-governance-mcp, A2A overview and MCP overview; policy guidance focuses on MCP tool requests, not A2A or long-running-task execution.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance controls table; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Spending policies are added at Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Cost Management > Configuration > + Add spending policy.
claims.quote:
In the Microsoft 365 admin center, go to Copilot > Cost Management.
2. Select the Configuration tab and then select + Add spending policy.

claims.claim: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies creates a spending policy.
claims.quote: For a group-scoped policy, follow the safe-create sequence: create the policy disabled, link its audience with Add assigned group, and let the service enable it once its requirements are satisfied.
claims.fix: Append to the spending-policy note: 'For a group-scoped policy, create it disabled, then link its audience using Add assigned group as described in the cited reference. Supplying nonempty assignedGroups during creation additionally requires CopilotCostManagement-Assignment.ReadWrite.All.' The printed create call alone does not attach a group.

claims.claim: Creating a spending policy without an initial audience requires delegated CopilotCostManagement-Policy.ReadWrite.All.
claims.quote: Creating a policy without an initial audience (assignedGroups omitted or empty) requires only CopilotCostManagement-Policy.ReadWrite.All.

claims.claim: Creating a spending policy through the API also requires Billing Administrator or Global Administrator.
claims.quote: At runtime, creating a policy also requires the Billing Administrator or Global Administrator directory role.

claims.claim: The create-policy body requires a concrete @odata.type, displayName, periodLimit, perUserLimit and serviceSettings.
claims.quote: In the request body, supply a JSON representation of a spendingPolicy object with a concrete @odata.type. Required properties are displayName, periodLimit, perUserLimit, and serviceSettings.

claims.claim: A spending policy created through this API is initially disabled.
claims.quote: A new policy is created disabled.
